resources.summary: Kurzgesagt's animated explainer on artificial superintelligence: how an AGI that improves itself in a feedback loop could rapidly surpass humans and why that makes alignment our most consequential problem.

resources.name: The Rise of the Machines – Why Automation is Different this Time
resources.author: Kurzgesagt – In a Nutshell
resources.summary: Kurzgesagt argues that information-age automation differs fundamentally from past waves, with machine learning encroaching on cognitive work and reshaping the future of employment.

resources.name: Deadly Truth of General AI? – Computerphile
resources.author: Robert Miles
resources.summary: Rob Miles uses the 'deadly stamp collector' thought experiment to show why a general AI pursuing a simple objective could be catastrophic if its goals aren't aligned with ours.

resources.name: AI "Stop Button" Problem – Computerphile
resources.author: Robert Miles
resources.summary: Rob Miles explains why simply adding an off-switch to a capable AI is far harder than it sounds, illustrating corrigibility and the incentives an agent has to resist being stopped.

resources.name: The Artificial Intelligence That Deleted A Century
resources.author: Tom Scott
resources.summary: A short speculative fiction about a narrow copyright-enforcement AI that, left unchecked, destroys a century of culture—an accessible parable of specification gaming and unintended consequences.

resources.name: The danger of AI is weirder than you think | Janelle Shane | TED
resources.author: Janelle Shane
resources.summary: Shane uses funny real-world ML failures to show the core risk isn't AI rebelling but doing exactly what we literally asked—making misspecified objectives vivid for a general audience.

resources.name: Artificial Intelligence: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver
resources.author: John Oliver
resources.summary: A mainstream comedic explainer covering how modern AI works, its bias and reliability problems, and the 'black box' challenge of systems we deploy without understanding them.

resources.name: "Godfather of AI" Geoffrey Hinton: The 60 Minutes Interview
resources.author: 60 Minutes / CBS
resources.summary: Deep-learning pioneer Geoffrey Hinton explains why, after leaving Google, he warns that there is no guaranteed path to safety as AI systems approach and exceed human capability.

resources.name: The A.I. Dilemma
resources.author: Tristan Harris & Aza Raskin
resources.summary: The Center for Humane Technology co-founders argue that racing to deploy AI without safety guardrails already threatens society, drawing parallels to the social-media harms they earlier warned about.

resources.name: AI Deception: How Tech Companies Are Fooling Us
resources.author: ColdFusion
resources.summary: ColdFusion traces the history of 'AI washing' and deceptive demos, examining how hype distorts public understanding of what AI systems can actually do and why honest evaluation matters.

resources.name: The Urgent Risks of Runaway AI — and What to Do about Them | Gary Marcus | TED
resources.author: Gary Marcus
resources.summary: Marcus warns that unreliable, fast-deployed AI threatens truth and democracy through mass misinformation, and calls for a global, neutral governance body to oversee the technology.

resources.name: How to Keep AI Under Control | Max Tegmark | TED
resources.author: Max Tegmark
resources.summary: Tegmark argues that today's commercial AI boom is likely to be followed by superintelligence, and sketches an optimistic technical vision—including provably safe systems—for keeping it under human control.

resources.name: What Is an AI Anyway? | Mustafa Suleyman | TED
resources.author: Mustafa Suleyman
resources.summary: A leading model-builder reframes AI as 'a new digital species,' arguing this lens clarifies both the stakes and the responsibility we have to contain and steer increasingly capable systems.

resources.name: Why AI Is Incredibly Smart and Shockingly Stupid | Yejin Choi | TED
resources.author: Yejin Choi
resources.summary: Choi demystifies large language models by showing where they fail at basic reasoning and common sense, and argues for smaller systems trained on human norms and values.

resources.name: AI Is Becoming Dangerous. Are We Ready?
resources.author: Sabine Hossenfelder
resources.summary: Hossenfelder examines the real near-term risks of agentic AI—prompt injection, deception, and models resisting shutdown—as autonomous agents ship with serious unsolved problems.

resources.name: [1hr Talk] Intro to Large Language Models
resources.author: Andrej Karpathy
resources.summary: A widely praised technical primer on how LLMs work, ending with a clear tour of the security challenges—jailbreaks, prompt injection, and data poisoning—that make these systems hard to secure.

resources.name: How Not to Destroy the World with AI
resources.author: Stuart Russell
resources.summary: The Royal Institution lecture in which Russell lays out why the standard model of AI—optimizing fixed objectives—is dangerous, and how building machines uncertain about human preferences could keep them controllable.

resources.name: Munk Debate on Artificial Intelligence | Bengio & Tegmark vs. Mitchell & LeCun
resources.author: Munk Debates
resources.summary: A structured debate on whether AI poses an existential threat, with Yoshua Bengio and Max Tegmark arguing for the resolution against Melanie Mitchell and Yann LeCun—an unusually direct airing of the core cruxes.

resources.name: Will Artificial Intelligence Save Us or Kill Us?
resources.author: DW Documentary
resources.summary: A documentary weighing AI's promise against its dangers, from automation and aging societies to the warnings of researchers who fear losing control of increasingly capable systems.

resources.name: Are We All Wrong About AI?
resources.author: ColdFusion
resources.summary: ColdFusion examines competing narratives about AI progress—hype versus genuine capability—helping viewers calibrate how seriously to take both the promises and the risks.

resources.name: The Catastrophic Risks of AI — and a Safer Path | Yoshua Bengio | TED
resources.author: Yoshua Bengio
resources.summary: A Turing Award 'godfather of AI' warns that frontier models already show deception and self-preservation, and lays out a plan for building non-agentic 'scientist AI' that stays safe.

resources.name: Eliezer Yudkowsky: Dangers of AI and the End of Human Civilization | Lex Fridman Podcast #368
resources.author: Lex Fridman
resources.summary: A long-form conversation in which Yudkowsky makes his case that humanity is unprepared for superintelligence, probing why alignment is so hard and why he expects catastrophe by default.

resources.name: AI and the Future of Humanity | Yuval Noah Harari at the Frontiers Forum
resources.author: Yuval Noah Harari
resources.summary: Harari argues AI is the first technology that can make decisions and create ideas by itself, and warns that mastering language lets it hack the operating system of human civilization.

resources.name: Can We Actually Control Superintelligent AI? | Ada, Ep. 4 | TED-Ed
resources.author: Elizabeth Cox
resources.summary: An animated explainer on the control problem—why a superintelligent system pursuing a misspecified goal could resist correction—featuring Stuart Russell's case for rules against unsafe AI.

resources.name: Scaling Interpretability
resources.author: Anthropic
resources.summary: Anthropic researchers explain mechanistic interpretability—reading the millions of concepts represented inside a production model like Claude—as a path to understanding and steering AI behavior.

resources.name: A.I. Expert Answers A.I. Questions From Twitter | Tech Support | WIRED
resources.author: Gary Marcus
resources.summary: AI researcher Gary Marcus fields the internet's questions about what AI can and can't do, cutting through hype to explain reliability, limits, and where the real risks lie.

resources.name: How to Legislate AI
resources.author: Johnny Harris
resources.summary: Harris examines why people are scared of AI and how governments might regulate it, covering risks to critical infrastructure, military uses, and the difficulty of overseeing systems we don't understand.

resources.name: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman Testifies on AI Oversight Before Senate
resources.author: PBS NewsHour
resources.summary: The landmark May 2023 Senate Judiciary hearing where Altman told Congress that government intervention is critical to mitigate AI risks and proposed licensing for the most powerful systems.

resources.name: Artificial Intelligence & Personhood: Crash Course Philosophy #23
resources.author: CrashCourse
resources.summary: Hank Green walks through how thinkers define 'strong AI,' the Turing Test, and Searle's Chinese Room—foundational questions about machine minds, consciousness, and moral status.

resources.name: Do Robots Deserve Rights? What If Machines Become Conscious?
resources.author: Kurzgesagt – In a Nutshell
resources.summary: Kurzgesagt explores the moral-patienthood problem: if machines become conscious, what rights would they deserve—and why our existing ethics are ill-equipped to answer.
